decisions.decision: Workflow execution: orchestrated pipeline or manual scripts?
decisions.context: Weekly forecasts need a repeatable path from data preparation through evaluation, while new model ideas should reach production quickly. Prioritized requirements: (1) reproduce past-week forecasts, (2) protect the weekly run, (3) shorten the path for model changes; the three-person team favors a manageable operating burden.

alternatives.label: Orchestrated ML pipeline
cons: Team effort: pipeline setup and upkeep

decisions.rationale: Past-week reproducibility and weekly-run reliability decide the choice: connected repeatable stages support consistent reruns. This costs the small team effort to set up and maintain the pipeline, but supports faster iteration once established.
consequences: Pipeline definitions and stages need ownership.
A failed stage can be isolated and rerun.

decisions.decision: How should model and pipeline changes be released?
decisions.context: New model ideas must reach production quickly without jeopardizing the weekly forecast run. Releases need a way to validate changes and restore a prior version if a production update causes trouble.

alternatives.label: Environment-gated deployment automation
cons: Fast iteration: approval gates add delay

decisions.rationale: Weekly-run reliability decides the choice: progressive rollout and rollback limit the impact of a bad update. This gives up some simplicity because release automation and rollback paths require maintenance; sources include “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and Azure’s “MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning.”
consequences: Keep the prior production model available for rollback.
Validate updates before full production use.

decisions.decision: How should past-week forecasts be reproducible?
decisions.context: The brief requires forecasts to be reproducible for any past week, which calls for retaining enough information to reconstruct the data, pipeline, and model used. The team also needs to compare new model ideas against known runs.
decisions.rationale: Past-week reproducibility decides the choice because preserving dataset versions, run snapshots, dependencies, and model metadata supports reconstruction across the lifecycle. This adds governance work for a small team; the rationale is supported by “MLOps: What It Is, Why it Matters, and How To Implement It (from a Data Scientist Perspective)” and Azure’s model management guidance.
consequences: Retain versioned datasets and run metadata.
Link deployed models to their training context.
Budget team time for lifecycle recordkeeping.

decisions.decision: How should candidate models be checked before promotion?
decisions.context: Quick model iteration still needs safeguards so a candidate does not damage the weekly forecast run. Evaluation thresholds provide a repeatable check against quality regression before promotion.

alternatives.label: Threshold-based quality regression testing
pros: Fast iteration: automated pass or fail
cons: Team effort: define and maintain thresholds

alternatives.label: Offline evaluation pipeline
pros: Reliability: checks candidates on held-out data
cons: Fast iteration: evaluation adds pipeline work

decisions.rationale: Weekly-run reliability decides the choice: explicit quality thresholds can prevent a regressing candidate from promotion while keeping the check automatable. The cost is agreeing on and maintaining suitable thresholds; Google’s “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “MLOps Principles” provide supporting evidence.
consequences: Define forecast quality metrics and acceptable thresholds.
Review thresholds as forecasting needs change.

decisions.context: The brief specifies weekly demand by store and product and gives no real-time serving requirement. Scheduled batch prediction fits the stated cadence and keeps the operating design focused on the weekly run.

alternatives.label: Scheduled batch prediction deployment
pros: Reliability: produces a forecast set per run

alternatives.label: Online computation serving
cons: Team effort: adds online serving operations

decisions.rationale: The weekly cadence and three-person team decide the choice: scheduled batch scoring aligns computation to the stated need without adding online serving operations. This gives up request-time freshness, which the brief does not require; sources include “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” and Azure’s model management guidance.
consequences: Publish a versioned forecast set after each scheduled run.
Consumers use the latest completed forecast set.
Set a schedule and recovery procedure for missed runs.

uncovered: Data ingestion source and mechanism; the brief does not identify upstream systems or delivery patterns.
Forecasting model family, training and tuning strategy, and the business metric used to select candidates.
Dataset retention period and the exact data, code, dependency, and environment snapshot needed to reproduce any past week.
Forecast delivery interface and downstream consumers.
Operational monitoring signals, alert thresholds, and ownership of weekly-run recovery.
